advances: The exact loss and common-center reserve concern ordinary planar halfspace incidence with arbitrary weights. The numerical corollary uses the special actual mixed chord weights.

proof:
Fix a positive-area corner $R_i$. A point of $\operatorname{int}A$ satisfies both strict inequalities defining the corner because the boundary of a convex body has area zero. Mixing this point with any point of the closed intersection proves the closure identity.

Pull back $R_i\cap A_t$ under the homothety. On the original $A$ the two thresholds become $(b_j-tv_j\cdot p)/(1-t)=b_j+t(b_j-v_j\cdot p)+O(t^2)$ for $j\ne i$. At the original pair of thresholds, the derivative of the area cut by the two less-than inequalities with respect to the $j$-th threshold is $\tau_{ij}$. Indeed, keeping the other threshold fixed, integrate over the signed strip parallel to the $j$-th cut. In the tangential coordinate the membership indicators have a pointwise limit except at the endpoints of the proper chord and at the single crossing of the two cut lines. Dominated convergence on a bounded projection of $A$, with the strip factor $1/\lVert v_j\rVert$, proves the partial derivative including the zero-length case. For simultaneous moves the correction to adding the two first-order changes is confined to the intersection of the two strips, of area $O(t^2)$ by invertibility of $x\mapsto(v_j\cdot x,v_\ell\cdot x)$. The expansion therefore holds for either sign of each threshold change. Multiplication by $(1-t)^2$ gives the exact loss. Its nonnegativity follows from $A_t\subseteq A$, and on $C_i$ the coefficients $b_j-v_j\cdot p$ are nonnegative. Minimizing this affine expression on compact $C_i$ gives the stated support value.

At every point of $A$ the weighted capture load is at least $\tau_2-\sum_i c_i\mathbf1_{R_i}$. This is immediate on a singleton from the definition of $c_i$, and every set of at least two captures has weight at least $\tau_2$. Integrate on $A\setminus A_t$. Each cap's loss divided by $t$ tends to $L_i(p)$ by the proper-section homothety formula in the weighted shell lemma, and each null corner contributes zero. Divide by $t$ and pass to the limit to get the weighted estimate. Its right side is affine in $p$, so maximizing on compact $A$ gives the single-center value. The one-deficient-corner and all-deficient-null cases follow from the individual bounds. In the one-corner case one can also see $D_j(p)\le 2r_j$ directly: for $p\in C_j$ the homothetic copy of $R_j$ lies in $A_t\cap R_j$, since a convex combination with positive weight on its strict point remains strict.

For the actual three-fiber configuration of the chord-weight theorem, the normals are pairwise independent because they span and sum to zero, and $\tau_2\ge\Lambda/4$. The traces cover $A$: for an interior point of $B$ all three strict support comparisons give $\sum_i b_i=-\sum_i h_i<0$, whereas a point missing all three would have $0<\sum_i b_i$. Thus the one-corner bound implies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)/\Lambda\ge(a-r_j)/2$, so $r_j\le a/9$ gives a loss of at least $4a/9$. If all deficient corners are null the bound is at least $a/2$.

statement:
Let $A\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a convex body, let $H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge b_i\}$ for $1\le i\le3$ cover $A$, and assume the normals are pairwise linearly independent and all cuts are proper. Write $a=|A|$, $U_i=|A\cap H_i|$, $a_i=\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_i\cdot x=b_i\})/\lVert v_i\rVert$, and $L_i(p)=2U_i+(b_i-v_i\cdot p)a_i$. For arbitrary positive weights $\lambda_i$ put $\Lambda=\sum_i\lambda_i$, $\tau_2=\Lambda-\max_i\lambda_i$, and $c_i=(\tau_2-\lambda_i)_+$. The region $R_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x<b_j\}$ is the region captured only by $H_i$. For each $i$ with $r_i=|R_i|>0$, set $C_i=\overline{R_i}$ and, for $j\ne i$, let $\ell$ be the third index and put
$$
\tau_{ij}=\frac{\mathcal H^1(A\cap\{v_j\cdot x=b_j,\ v_\ell\cdot x\le b_\ell\})}{\lVert v_j\rVert}.
$$
Then $C_i=A\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{v_j\cdot x\le b_j\}$. For every $p\in A$ and $A_t=p+(1-t)(A-p)$ the exact right loss is
$$
D_i(p)=\lim_{t\downarrow0}\frac{|R_i\setminus A_t|}{t}
=2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}(b_j-v_j\cdot p)\tau_{ij}\ge0.
$$
It satisfies $D_i(p)\le2r_i$ on $C_i$ and its minimum there is attained and equals
$$
2r_i-\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
-h_{C_i}\Bigl(-\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr),
$$
where $h_C$ is the support function of $C$.

With null corners omitted, for every $p\in A$,
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-\sum_i c_iD_i(p).
$$
The right side attains its maximum at one common $p\in A$, with value
$$
2a\tau_2-2\sum_i c_ir_i+\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}b_j\tau_{ij}
+h_A\Bigl(-\sum_i c_i\sum_{j\ne i}\tau_{ij}v_j\Bigr).
$$
If just one positive-area corner $R_j$ has $c_j>0$, every $p\in C_j$ satisfies $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge 2a\tau_2-2(\tau_2-\lambda_j)r_j$. If all deficient corners are null, $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(p)\ge2a\tau_2$ for every $p\in A$.

In the actual mixed setting of the critical chord-weight theorem, these one-corner and all-deficient-null estimates imply a normalized loss of at least $(a-r_j)/2$ and $a/2$, respectively, after dividing by $\Lambda$. In particular $r_j\le a/9$ gives a normalized loss of at least $4a/9$ at every $p\in C_j$.
title: Exact losses of planar singleton corners and an attained common contraction center
